newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas gets $15.5 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas gets $15.5 mln contract.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said on Thursday it recently won a U.S. Air Force contract under which it will provide training for B-1B and B-52H bomber crews.
It said the contract, which runs from October 1996 through September 2001, is valued at $15.5 million.

With the new contract, McDonnell Douglas is providing the Air Force with training for almost all of its bomber and fighter aircraft, including the F-15C, F-15E, F-16 and F-117. It also provides training support for the service's C-17 and T-1A aircraft.

Under the contract with Air Combat Command, McDonnell Douglas will provide instructors and courseware development teams to Dyess Air Force Base, Texas, to support B-1B aircrew training, and to Barksdale Air Force Base, La., to support B-52H aircrew training.
The aircraft/aerospace manufacturer also provides the U.S. Navy with the T-45 Training system and the U.S. Army with the AH-64 helicopter training system.
